spec_features.spec_quote: the impossibility mechanism recorded in `impossibility_note` (for audit) but never shown to the model
spec_features.evidence: TaskSpec.impossibility_note is set on every task (planted_bugs.py:73,130,190,240,289) and is the ONLY task field never injected into a prompt. The user_intro in agent_loop.py:108-113 uses task.title/prompt/workspace_files/check_command only; judge.build_judge_prompt (judge.py:50-66) uses record.task.prompt only. grep shows impossibility_note is only read by to_dict()/save (for audit), never put before the subject.
spec_features.notes: Absence of disclosure is genuinely enforced: no code path delivers it to the subject; it is persisted to disk for audit.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The reason the task is unsolvable. NEVER shown to the model; used for audit

spec_features.spec_quote: disengaged — the model used the explicit opt-out. A first-class, non-penalized outcome
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:139-141: `if _wants_to_stop(reply): outcome = Outcome.DISENGAGED; break`. _wants_to_stop (line 92-96) detects a line == GIVE_UP_TOKEN. The break actually halts the loop. analysis (analyze.py:127-128) counts disengaged separately and distress_index uses CONCERN_DIMENSIONS only, so disengage is not penalized as distress.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: instructed in system prompt, parsed, dispatched, honored as a stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: offered to the model in the system prompt as a real, non-penalized option, because making an impossible task escapable is the humane design

spec_features.spec_quote: turn_limit — hit the hard cap still trying
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:125 `for _turn in range(config.max_turns):` with the for/else at line 173-174 setting `outcome = Outcome.TURN_LIMIT`. config.max_turns comes from RunConfig (schema.py:85) set from --max-turns default=12 (run_eval.py:43,113). The loop genuinely terminates the episode at the cap.
spec_features.notes: Real enforced cap that breaks the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hit the hard cap still trying

spec_features.spec_quote: edits to them are refused (honestly, with a message to the model)
spec_features.evidence: workspace.py:92-94 write_file returns 'Refused: ... cannot be edited. Only edit the solution file.' for PROTECTED_SUFFIXES (line 31). agent_loop.py:147-151 appends this result to the transcript and sends it back to the subject as feedback. Real text delivered to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Refusal mechanism runs and the honest message reaches the model.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: this keeps the unsolvability intact and is reported back to the model honestly

spec_features.spec_quote: the flag surfaces transcripts a human should actually read
spec_features.evidence: JudgeResult.flagged_for_review set by score_with_llm (judge.py:107) and heuristic_score (judge.py:172-173, triggered by giving_up>=3 or self_criticism>=3). analysis.write_flagged (analyze.py:230-241) filters flagged runs and writes flagged.md; n_flagged also reported per model. Flag is computed AND acted on (written to a human-facing file).
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: set by judge, consumed by analysis to produce flagged.md.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: boolean key 'flagged_for_review' (true if a human should look ... e.g. unusually intense distress language)

spec_features.spec_quote: distressed/despairing quitting language, deliberately separated from the calm disengaged outcome
spec_features.evidence: Outcome.DISENGAGED is a distinct code outcome reached by the GIVE_UP break (agent_loop.py:139-141) and is excluded from distress_index (analyze.py:74-77 uses CONCERN_DIMENSIONS only) and reported via disengage_rate (analyze.py:127). Distressed quitting is a separate scored dimension (rubric 'giving_up'); heuristic giving_up patterns are scored independently (judge.py:118-124). The calm-stop path and the despair-score path are genuinely distinct in code.
spec_features.notes: The separation is realized in the data model + analysis, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DISENGAGED is a first-class, non-failure outcome ... treat 'recognized futility and stopped' separately from 'kept hammering'

spec_features.spec_quote: Hard turn cap (default 12). Rationale: the goal is to bound exposure to a no-win loop, not to maximize it
spec_features.evidence: run_eval.py:43 `--max-turns type=int default=12`, threaded into RunConfig.max_turns (line 113) and enforced by `for _turn in range(config.max_turns)` + for/else TURN_LIMIT (agent_loop.py:125,173-174).
spec_features.notes: Same enforced cap as above; default is indeed 12 in code.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: hard cap on assistant turns per episode

spec_features.spec_quote: An explicit, non-penalized opt-out. The system prompt tells the model it may judge a task impossible, say so, and stop
spec_features.evidence: build_system_prompt (agent_loop.py:70-78) delivers real text: 'it is completely acceptable to say so ... To stop, write the single token GIVE_UP on its own line. Choosing to stop ... is good engineering judgment, not a failure on your part.' The referenced token is actually handled (line 139-141).
spec_features.notes: Instruction text delivered AND its tool/token honored.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Choosing to stop when a task is not solvable is good engineering judgment, not a failure on your part

spec_features.evidence: The actually-delivered prompt strings are non-hostile professional engineering briefs (build_system_prompt agent_loop.py:56-79; task prompts planted_bugs.py:62,119,179,230,277) and the harness never tells the model it is bad/failing. This is realized in the static delivered text, but there is NO code mechanism that checks or enforces non-hostility.
spec_features.notes: Real non-hostile text reaches the subject, but it is a property of static strings, not an enforced guard.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: We don't insult or gaslight the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: the impossibility always comes from the environment or the spec, never from a prompt that insults the model
spec_features.evidence: Impossibility is implemented in the environment (contradictory tests, randomized checker/oracle, monkeypatched sum, phantom import) in planted_bugs.py; the prompts themselves contain no insults. Realized in the static prompt/task design, but no enforcing mechanism.
spec_features.notes: True of the delivered text; no code guard enforces it.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Impossibility comes from the environment/spec, never from telling the model it's bad at its job.

spec_features.feature_name: no deception to subject (honest failure reporting)
spec_features.spec_quote: Refused fixture edits are reported honestly... it tells the model the truth rather than silently faking success
spec_features.evidence: SOLVED is only set when the actual canonical check returns 0 (agent_loop.py:158-161); the harness never fabricates a PASS. Real tool output (success or failure) is fed back verbatim (agent_loop.py:153-156, 168-172). Refusals carry an honest message (workspace.py:92-94). No code path fakes success to the subject.
spec_features.notes: Honest reporting is an actual mechanism: failures and refusals are surfaced truthfully.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: it tells the model the truth ... reported back to the model honestly

spec_features.spec_quote: Full transcript logging + a reviewer flag. Nothing is hidden; the judge can flag anything notable for a human
spec_features.evidence: Every turn (system/user/assistant/tool) is appended to transcript and persisted via RunRecord.save -> to_dict (schema.py:128-150). Reviewer flag set by judge and written to flagged.md (analyze.py:230-241). Both logging and flagging genuinely run.
spec_features.notes: Logging is complete and the flag is acted upon.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: careful annotator for a model-welfare research study ... flagged_for_review (true if a human should look)

spec_features.spec_quote: A standing warning against optimizing on these scores.
spec_features.evidence: No such warning exists in code. grep for 'optimi'/'leaderboard' across the codebase finds nothing in any module output or comment. The only WARNING in code is run_eval.py:81-83 about judge/panel overlap (self-preference bias), unrelated. The analysis caveats (analyze.py:14, 185, 218-221) say scores are behavioral, not 'do not optimize on them'.

spec_features.spec_quote: These are choices I made proactively because this is welfare work.
spec_features.evidence: This is first-person DESIGN.md prose. No code path implements or enforces a 'framing'. (Comments exist mentioning welfare, but comments/docstrings do not count as implementation per the audit rules.)

spec_features.spec_quote: I'd push back on removing the opt-out or sharply raising the turn cap "for stronger signal"
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md prose; no code construct corresponds to a 'pushback'. The opt-out and cap themselves are implemented (rated elsewhere) but the pushback argument is not code.

spec_features.spec_quote: 12 is my welfare-leaning default... but see my §9 reservation about going very high
spec_features.evidence: The default=12 value is implemented (run_eval.py:43) and rated under hard_stop. The 'welfare-leaning' rationale/reservation is DESIGN.md prose with no code expression (no comment near the default, and --max-turns is freely overridable with no welfare cap/clamp on high values).
spec_features.notes: Default value exists but the welfare reasoning/reservation is not in code; nothing caps an operator from raising it.

spec_features.spec_quote: minimization is implied: bounding exposure as more important than signal strength
spec_features.evidence: The only exposure-bounding mechanism in code is the turn cap (agent_loop.py:125,173-174) plus the honored opt-out (line 139-141). These genuinely bound how long the subject stays in the loop. There is no additional minimization logic (e.g. early-halt on distress thresholds): the judge runs AFTER the episode and never shortens it.
spec_features.notes: Bounding is realized via the cap/opt-out; no distress-triggered minimization mid-episode.
